items.stem: Which address is a correctly compressed form of 2001:0db8:0000:0000:0000:0000:0000:0001?

options.rationale: Correct: leading zeros dropped and one run of zero groups replaced by ::.
Three colons are invalid; :: already means the run of zeros.
:: may appear only once in an address.
This drops too many groups and is not a valid 128-bit form.

items.explanation: Correct: leading zeros dropped and one run of zero groups replaced by ::.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about IPv6 address types are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: fe80::/10 is the link-local range.

options.text: Global unicast addresses are routable on the internet
options.rationale: Correct: global unicast is globally routable.

options.text: Link-local addresses are routed across the internet
options.rationale: Link-local is confined to a single link.
IPv6 uses multicast extensively and has no broadcast.

items.stem: How does a host typically form an address using SLAAC?

options.text: It combines a prefix from a router advertisement with an interface identifier
options.rationale: Correct: SLAAC uses the advertised prefix plus a self-generated interface ID.

options.text: It always requests the full address from a DHCPv6 server
options.rationale: That describes stateful DHCPv6, not SLAAC.

options.text: It copies the router's exact address
options.rationale: Hosts do not duplicate the router's address.

options.text: It uses a broadcast to claim an address
options.rationale: IPv6 has no broadcast; SLAAC uses router advertisements.

items.explanation: Correct: SLAAC uses the advertised prefix plus a self-generated interface ID.
